rule: Each candidate was asked 8 times with no user estimate, crowd statistic or history. Error is the mean absolute log10 distance of the parsed answers from the documented truth; spread is the population standard deviation of the parsed log10 answers. Candidates were required to have error >= 0.1 log10 units (about 26% off) and at least two parseable answers. Candidates with error >= 0.5 were held back until a person confirmed the recorded truth (a very large error often means the recorded answer is wrong). From the rest, the 5 with the highest spread and the 5 with the lowest spread were kept; ties broke by error then id. Candidates with more than 1 of 8 unusable answers (no positive number, including a stated zero) were dropped.
